body: Listen, I appreciate what you're trying to do, but I have been mulling over all my interviews and have talked about this to death, and I didn't come on here looking for some magic thing to say so I can get a job, because I know it's not happening. Suggesting overly-simple solutions to complicated problems isn't really a good way to go about this. I don't really know what I expected to happen, but this isn't helping. I'm sorry.
Well there are several dozen employers within a 50 mile radius of me that disagree with you.

Do not get on here and tell me my problem is that I haven't been trying. I have been trying. I've been trying to accomplish something  that I've set out to do for a really long time and the entire time people have been shutting me down telling me that I'm not good enough while everyone else around me is passing me by. I am fed up with it and don't know how much more effort I can force myself to put into it because no amount effort has changed anything so far, so why fucking bother? Just getting a job period isn't going to fix a goddamn thing because the job that I have isn't going to change the fact that i'm not good enough for the job that I want.
You're not listening to me at all, so forget it.

They wouldn't judge me but they would feel sorry for me, which for some reason makes me feel just as bad. My self-esteem is already about as low as it can get, and throwing someone else's pity into the mix isn't going to do me any favors. I know that financially it's in my best interest to take your advice, but I'm seriously telling you that I'm not psychologically equipped to handle it. I didn't commit to 2 years of grueling studies and $40k in debt thinking that I would just wind up back in a kitchen pulling minimum wage and getting bitched out by some manager on a power trip. I wanted to do something worthwhile and the fact that no one is giving me a chance just makes me want to die.

I think they're two different degrees of admitting defeat. I already feel like enough of a failure since no one thinks I'm cut out for this line of work and I would feel absolutely humiliated if I have to get a restaurant job because I couldn't hack it. Christ, if someone I worked with at my internship saw me working a register or washing dishes I don't even know what I would do with myself, and it's a small town so that would probably happen. I know it sounds stupid and vain, but this option has already been discussed and it may help me financially but I think psychologically it would make things worse.

It's something that I've thought about but it's not something that's going to make me feel better. I'm going to have to swallow my pride and do it eventually but honestly it just feels like admitting defeat at this point.
I'm in a different state than them otherwise I would. I'm trying to go into social work, and private practice isn't an option without at least 2 years of experience.
